RESOLUTION NO. ______
A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF MILPITAS
AUTHORIZING THE PURCHASE OF ONE (1) PIERCE MANUFACTURING, INC.
VELOCITY HEAVY DUTY RESCUE VEHICLE FROM GOLDEN STATE FIRE
APPARATUS, INC., FOR THE TOTAL NOT-TO- EXCEED AMOUNT OF $1,560,614.00,
PURSUANT TO A COOPERATIVE PROCUREMENT CONTRACT THROUGH
SOURCEWELL, A STATE OF MINNESOTA LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNIT AND
SERVICE COOPERATIVE
WHEREAS, Section I-2-3.05 (“Public Agency Purchases”) of the Milpitas Municipal Code authorizes the
City’s Purchasing Agent to make such purchases based on an agreement or cooperative purchasing program entered
into by any public agency regardless of whether the City is a named party to the agreement or an actual participant
in such a program, provided that: (1) the underlying purchase was made using competitive negotiation or bidding
procedures at least as restrictive as the City’s, and may include nationally bid cooperative contracts, (2) the public
agency is a “public agency” as defined in Government Code section 6500; and
WHEREAS, Municipal Code Section I-2-3.05 (“Public Agency Purchases”) specifies that the Purchasing
Agent may arrange for the City to enter into purchase contracts with a supplier or contractor for the purchase of
supplies or services, the pricing and terms of which have been previously established by another public agency or
improved pricing and terms, provided that the Purchasing Agent determines that such purchase contracts are in the
City's best interest; and
WHEREAS, on July 2, 2025, Sourcewell (Sourcewell), a State of Minnesota local government unit and
service cooperative, issued a Request for Proposal (RFP) #082025 entitled “Firefighting Apparatus and Fire Service
Vehicles”; and
WHEREAS, on January 6, 2026, Sourcewell awarded Contract No. 082025-PMI to Pierce Manufacturing,
Inc. (Pierce) pursuant to the RFP; and
WHEREAS, Pierce is a manufacturer that sells its products through 16 authorized dealerships located
throughout the United States, each of which is contracted with Pierce for a designated territory; and
WHEREAS, Golden State Fire Apparatus Inc., is the exclusive authorized dealer for Pierce’s Central and
Northern California territory; and
WHEREAS, the Milpitas Fire Department’s current Urban Search and Rescue Apparatus (USAR86) is 26
years old and has exceeded its useful lifespan by several years and, accordingly, staff wishes to purchase a
replacement USAR from Golden State Fire Apparatus Inc., for the total not-to- exceed amount of $1,560,614.00,
as specified in the terms of their competitive cost proposal; and
WHEREAS, the total proposed by Golden State Fire Apparatus Inc. includes a discount of approximately
13% off the manufacturer’s suggested retail price if the purchase is 100% pre-paid, and represents an additional
7.5% savings off Pierce’s contracted Sourcewell pricing; and
WHEREAS, the City’s Purchasing Agent, in accordance with the City’s Municipal Code Section 1-2-3.05,
has reviewed all of the documentation related to Sourcewell RFP #082025, and original contract awarded to Pierce
Manufacturing, Inc. (082025-PMI), and has confirmed that the RFP competitive process was consistent with, and
at least as restrictive as, the City’s procurement processes.
NOW, THEREFORE, the City Council of the City of Milpitas hereby finds, determines, and resolves as
follows:
1. The City Council has duly considered the full record before it, which may include but is not limited
to such things as the City staff report, testimony by staff and the public, and other materials and
1 Resolution No. xxxx
evidence submitted or provided to it. Furthermore, the recitals set forth above are found to be true
and correct and are incorporated herein by reference.
2. The City Manager, or Designee, is authorized to negotiate and execute a purchase order purchase
one (1) Pierce Manufacturing Inc. Velocity Heavy Duty Rescue Vehicle for the Fire Department
from Golden State Fire Apparatus, Inc., the exclusive authorized dealer for Piece’s Central and
Northern California territory, through Pierce’s cooperative contract with Sourcewell (082025-
PMI), for the total not-to-exceed amount of $1,560,614.

attachments.name: AR_Purchase of Heavy Duty Rescue Vehicle
attachments.text:
CITY OF MILPITAS
AGENDA REPORT
(AR)
Item Title: Authorize the City Manager, or Designee, to Negotiate and Execute a Purchase
Order with Golden State Fire Apparatus, Inc. for Purchase of the Pierce
Manufacturing, Inc. Velocity Heavy Duty Rescue Vehicle (Staff Contact: Luz
Cofresí-Howe, Finance Director, 408-586-3111; and Jason Schoonover, Fire
Department Chief, 408-586-2811)
Category: Consent Calendar-Community Services and Sustainable Infrastructure
Meeting Date: 3/17/2026
Recommendation: Adopt a resolution authorizing the City Manager, or designee, to negotiate and
execute a Purchase Order with Golden State Fire Apparatus, Inc. to purchase one (1)
Pierce Manufacturing, Inc. Velocity Heavy Duty Rescue Vehicle for a not-to-exceed
amount of $1,560,614, which includes vehicle cost, sales tax, California tire fee, and
payment and performance bonds.
BACKGROUND:
In Fiscal Year 2025-2026, the City programmed Capital Improvement Program (CIP) Project 3475 – Urban
Search and Rescue (USAR) Vehicle. The National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) Standard 1901 Annex D
for Fire Apparatus recommends all fire apparatus be completely removed from emergency service at 25 years.
The Fire Department’s current Urban Search and Rescue Apparatus (USAR86) is 26 years old and has
exceeded its useful lifespan by several years. Due to the age of the current USAR, required maintenance time
and costs continue to increase, which can significantly impact the City’s emergency response capabilities.
ANALYSIS:
On July 2, 2025, Sourcewell, a State of Minnesota local government unit and service cooperative, issued a
Request for Proposal (RFP) #082025 Firefighting Apparatus and Fire Service Vehicles. On January 6, 2026,
Sourcewell awarded Contract No. 082025-PMI to Pierce Manufacturing, Inc. (Pierce) pursuant to the RFP. The
City’s Purchasing Agent, in accordance with City Municipal Code Section I-2-3.05, which authorizes the
Purchasing Agent to make purchases based upon an agreement or cooperative purchasing program entered
into by another public agency, reviewed the Sourcewell RFP and awarded contract, and confirmed the RFP
competitive process was consistent with, and at least as restrictive as, the City’s procurement processes.
Pierce only manufactures products, and does not sell directly to end-customers. Instead, Pierce sells its
products through sixteen (16) authorized dealerships located throughout the United States, each of which is
contracted with Pierce for a designated territory. Golden State Fire Apparatus, Inc. is Pierce’s exclusive
authorized dealer for Central and Northern California. Golden State Fire Apparatus, Inc. provided a competitive
cost proposal that offers a discount of approximately 13% off the manufacturer’s suggested retail price if the
purchase is 100% pre-paid. This discount also represents an additional 7.5% savings off Pierce’s contracted
Sourcewell pricing. As such, staff recommends issuing a purchase order to Golden State Fire Apparatus, Inc.,
as Pierce’s only authorized dealer in our region, for the purchase of a Pierce Velocity Heavy Duty Rescue
Vehicle for a not-to-exceed amount of $1,560,614.
If approved, the new USAR apparatus will consolidate and centralize heavy rescue inventory and equipment
that is currently distributed across three separate trailers. Bringing these resources together on a single,
purpose-built apparatus will significantly improve response times by eliminating the need to locate, hitch, and
transport multiple trailers to an incident scene. The community risk profile within the City – which includes
major freeway corridors, multi-story commercial and residential structures, and active construction sites –
requires the Fire Department to be trained, equipped, and prepared to respond to a wide range of technical
rescue incidents at any moment. Past incidents in Milpitas have included motor vehicle accidents on freeways
involving tractor-trailer trucks, mechanical shoring of unstable structures, and deployment of complex rope-
rescue systems. The new USAR apparatus will support response to incidents such as structure collapses,
high-angle rope rescue (including highline systems), confined-space rescue (permit-required environments),
and mass transportation emergencies. The purchase will also bring the City into compliance with the
recommendations of NFPA Standard 1901, Annex D, for fire apparatus.
POLICY ALTERNATIVE(S):
Alternative 1: Do not negotiate and execute a Purchase Order with Golden State Fire Apparatus, Inc. for the
purchase of a Pierce Velocity Heavy Duty Rescue Vehicle.
Pros: The City would not expend these funds.
Cons: The time and costs associated with maintaining the Fire Department’s existing heavy rescue vehicle will
continue to increase, as its useful lifespan has already been exceeded. This could also significantly restrict the
City’s emergency response capabilities.
Reason for Not Recommending: NFPA Standard 1901 Annex D for Fire Apparatus recommends all fire
apparatus be completely removed from emergency service at 25 years. The Fire Department’s current
USAR86 is 26 years old and has exceeded its useful lifespan by several years. This has and will continue to
result in increased time and costs required to maintain it. The Fire Department is not confident the current
apparatus can continue to reliably function in its current capacity. The anticipated delivery of the apparatus
from time of order is estimated to be up to four years. Therefore, purchase of the new USAR is important to
ensure optimal rescue responsiveness and capabilities.
FISCAL IMPACT:
As part of the 2026-2030 Adopted CIP (Project No. 3475), funding of $1,850,000 was approved for the
purchase of an Urban Search and Rescue vehicle (USAR) for the Fire Department.
Golden State Fire Apparatus, Inc. provided three pricing options. Staff recommend Option A (100%
prepayment at time of order), which offers the greatest savings to the City:
Option A – Option B – Option C –
100% Prepayment Payment at Delivery 50% Prepayment
Grand Total $1,560,614 $1,796,411 $1,656,700
Savings vs. Option B $235,797 (13.1%) — $139,711 (7.8%)
The Option A grand total of $1,560,614 includes the vehicle ($1,423,222 after a 13.3% prepayment discount),
sales tax ($133,427), California tire fee ($11), and a 100% payment and performance bond ($3,954). Payment
is due within 30 calendar days of contract execution, with delivery estimated 42-45 months thereafter.
To protect the City's prepayment over the manufacturing period, the purchase includes payment and
performance bonds issued by a surety company. The performance bond guarantees the dealer will deliver the
completed vehicle to specification, or the City will be compensated up to the full contract value if the dealer or
manufacturer fails to perform due to default, insolvency, or other cause. The payment bond protects the City
from third-party claims arising from the dealer's failure to pay its subcontractors or suppliers. Per the proposal
specifications, the issuing surety must carry a minimum A.M. Best financial strength rating of A- (Excellent) and
be listed on the U.S. Treasury Department's Circular 570 list of approved sureties. Payment shall not be
remitted until the City has received and verified the executed bonds.
The purchase price is within the approved CIP appropriation, resulting in a remaining balance of $289,386. The
proposal also includes a $25,000 contingency reserve fund for change orders during manufacturing; any
unused portion will be credited back to the City. Staff will evaluate the remaining balance upon delivery and
recommend reallocation or return to the Equipment Replacement Fund through a future budget process.
No additional appropriation is required. There is no impact on the General Fund.
CALIFORNIA ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY ACT (CEQA):
The action has no potential for resulting in either a direct physical change in the environment, or a reasonably
foreseeable indirect physical change in the environment and is not a project pursuant to Pub. Resources Code,
§ 21065 and Cal. Code Regs., tit. 14, § 15378. Even if a project, the action is exempt from further CEQA
review pursuant to Cal. Code Regs., tit. 14, § 15061(b)(3) as it can be seen with certainty that there is no
possibility that the activity in question may have a significant effect on the environment.
ATTACHMENT(S):
(a) Resolution
(b) Proposal from Golden State Fire Apparatus, Inc.
